text: Why are intelligent people sexually deviant? And this question comes to us when there is a scandal, that Abhileena gets exposed, the famous intellectual gets exposed, or the politician gets exposed. And suddenly people start wondering, why does this happen to the people at the top? And but here's the interesting part. Psychologists have found very little evidence that intelligence itself makes someone sexually deviant. But what they have found is something even more dangerous, which is power. According to psychologists, Dasha Keltner, power often creates what he calls empathy deficit. The more powerful people become, the less sensitive they can become to the feelings of others. Rules start feeling optional and boundary start feeling negotiable. And then there is something called moral licensing. When someone sees themselves as brilliant, successful, influential and historically important, they sometimes start believing they have earned the right to break rules in other areas of life, not consciously but psychologically. And that is why many researchers don't look at these scandals as a story about intelligence. They look at them as a combination of desire, opportunity, status and lack of accountability. Think about it. Most people never get the chance to abuse power. The rich, the famous and the influential, they have access, protection and networks that ordinary people don't. And that is where another concept comes up, the dark trial. The narcissism, Macchivalinism and psychopathy. Traits that can actually help people climb hierarchies while simultaneously making people manipulate easily. And which is why the real question is, why are intelligent people sexually deviant is not important? What happens when intelligence, power, status, opportunity and the belief that you are above the rules all exist in the same person? And if you want to go deeper into this, read the power paradox by Dasha Keltener, the Lucifer effect by Philip Jimbardo.
